headlineRead: The strongest new macro evidence is the August US payroll rebound. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000, unemployment held at 4.1%, June/July were revised up by a combined 55,000, and wage growth was 3.1% year over year. Combined with August ISM Services at 55.4, Prices 72.6 and record diesel costs, this pushes the regime away from yesterday's tactical rate-relief narrative and back toward resilient demand plus inflation/rate risk. The 10-year reached about 4.81% and September hike pricing rose materially. Copper also moved sharply higher in the research hierarchy as tariff-driven US inventory accumulation leaves ex-US exchange stocks thin. AI/power physical capex remains structurally strong. Gold's Sep 3 tactical confirmation weakened after payrolls. Samsara becomes a new differentiated priority-research candidate for physical-operations software after 30% revenue/ARR growth and a fourth consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter, but it is not chased after the earnings gap.
whatsNewNow: August US nonfarm payrolls increased 162,000 with unemployment 4.1%; June and July revisions added a combined 55,000 jobs. Average hourly earnings rose 0.3% month over month and 3.1% year over year.

The jobs surprise pushed the US 10-year to roughly 4.81% and the 2-year to roughly 4.37%; September hike probabilities moved back toward the high-50s/around 60%. This reverses part of the Sep 3 Waller relief.

Brent settled $92.68 and WTI $91.48 after a sharply higher week; US diesel averaged a record roughly $5.85/gal while Hormuz vessel traffic remained exceptionally depressed. Refined-product inflation remains the stronger transmission signal than crude alone.

Copper supply geography moved materially up the hierarchy: tariff-driven US inventory accumulation is thinning ex-US stocks, with LME copper near record territory and Shanghai inventories around their lowest since early 2024. This is a physical-buffer problem, not merely an AI narrative.

Tesla fell roughly 6% after NHTSA opened an Audit Query into Cybercab self-certification following Austin commercial deployment. This is a new company-specific risk/next test but does not yet justify changing the 61/C fundamentals score.

Samsara reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $508.4M (+30% YoY), ending ARR of $2.125B (+30%), net new ARR +28%, and a fourth consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter. It enters priority research as a differentiated physical-operations/automation software candidate; valuation and post-earnings entry still need work.

Gold fell about 1.2% to roughly $4,419 after the payroll report pushed yields and the dollar higher. The structural hedge thesis remains intact, but the tactical Sep 3 confirmation is no longer strong enough for a top-five theme rank.
whatMattersMostNow: Resilient jobs/services demand + hot prices keeping Fed and long-end risk alive
Refined-product/diesel inflation and Hormuz physical disruption
Copper ex-US inventory squeeze / tariff distortion
AI/power transmission-generation capex and time-to-power bottlenecks
Funded-load quality and structurally expensive capital
Gold/precious metals as a structural hedge but tactically rate-sensitive

macro.regime: Resilient US growth plus persistent energy/services inflation and restrictive long rates. Physical AI/grid capex remains strong, but the hurdle rate for leveraged duration rose again after payrolls.
macro.rates: US 10Y reached ~4.81% and 2Y ~4.37% after payrolls. The last verified 10Y breakeven reference is ~2.35%; exact live term-premium and CCC ticks were not manufactured. Prior CCC ~14.6% remains explicitly dated.
macro.energy: Brent $92.68 and WTI $91.48 Sep 4 settle; US diesel roughly $5.85/gal record. Hormuz transit remains abnormally low and middle-distillate scarcity remains the main inflation channel.
macro.labour: NFP +162k; unemployment 4.1%; participation 61.6%; wages +3.1% YoY. This improves broad labour evidence despite ISM Services Employment remaining contractionary at 47.8.
macro.risk: S&P -0.38%, Dow -0.51%, Nasdaq -0.29% after payrolls. Semiconductors outperformed while consumer discretionary weakened. This is modest risk-off, not a broad liquidation.
macro.gold: Spot gold fell ~1.2% to ~$4,419 after yields/USD rose; structural fiscal/geopolitical hedge logic remains but near-term confirmation weakened.

ism.status: Official August Manufacturing and Services reports reverified; no monthly data changed from the Sep 4 snapshot, so ism-macro-snapshot.json was not churned for timestamp only.
ism.powerStackRead: Official ISM continues to validate real transmission/generation long-lead purchasing plus electrical/electronic/memory shortages. The new NFP evidence raises confidence in aggregate demand but also raises the rate/inflation hurdle. Prefer order-backed pricing power and cash conversion.

developingThemes.name: Resilient Jobs/Services + Hot Inflation / Fed Risk
developingThemes.whyNow: NFP +162k and upward revisions arrive on top of ISM Services 55.4 and Prices 72.6.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Raises short/long yields and USD, compresses duration, weakens gold tactically and keeps financing costs elevated even as real demand stays firm.
developingThemes.confirmation: PPI/CPI remain sticky and long yields stay high.
developingThemes.invalidation: Inflation cools sharply and jobs momentum fades without a growth shock.
developingThemes.nextTest: Sep 10 PPI, Sep 11 CPI, Sep 15-16 FOMC.
developingThemes.action: Favor cash-generative pricing-power businesses over leveraged duration.

developingThemes.name: Refined-Product / Diesel Inflation + Hormuz
developingThemes.whyNow: Diesel is at record retail levels while Hormuz traffic remains exceptionally depressed despite high refinery utilisation.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Raises freight, agriculture and consumer costs; supports refiners/integrated energy but eventually destroys demand.
developingThemes.confirmation: Distillate inventories/cracks remain extreme and Hormuz transit stays impaired.
developingThemes.invalidation: Rapid transit/inventory normalisation collapses product spreads.
developingThemes.nextTest: EIA distillates, refinery outages, Hormuz/Russia flows.
developingThemes.action: Prefer quality integrated/refining exposure; no geopolitical chase.

developingThemes.name: Copper Ex-US Inventory Squeeze / Tariff Distortion
developingThemes.whyNow: US tariff-driven stockpiling is pulling refined copper away from other markets while LME/Shanghai visible buffers tighten and LME prices approach record territory.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports copper miners and pricing power across scarce electrical equipment while raising cable, transformer and contractor input costs.
developingThemes.confirmation: Ex-US inventories keep falling and backwardation/tight spreads persist.
developingThemes.invalidation: Tariff arbitrage unwinds and refined supply replenishes LME/Asia inventories quickly.
developingThemes.nextTest: LME/CME/Shanghai inventory geography, US tariff policy and FCX/BHP production guidance.
developingThemes.action: FCX preferred near $70-72; BHP diversified exposure; do not capitalise squeeze pricing permanently.

developingThemes.name: AI / Power / Transmission Long-Lead Capex
developingThemes.whyNow: ISM public respondent evidence directly confirms transmission/generation material purchasing and long-lead planning.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports grid equipment, contractors, power management, cooling and time-to-power suppliers independently of near-term software sentiment.
developingThemes.confirmation: Backlogs, deposits, named projects and FCF conversion continue rising.
developingThemes.invalidation: Funded-load audits translate into supplier cancellations/backlog deterioration.
developingThemes.action: Maintain quality leaders; entry discipline remains mandatory.

developingThemes.name: AI Funded-Load Quality + Capital Competition
developingThemes.whyNow: Strong jobs and structurally high capital demand keep financing expensive while utilities continue screening speculative load queues.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Rewards named customers/deposits/backlog and penalizes pre-revenue or heavily financed AI/nuclear projects.
developingThemes.confirmation: Real yields stay elevated and projects increasingly require deposits/customer funding.
developingThemes.invalidation: Sustained real-yield collapse plus broad funded-load conversion.
developingThemes.nextTest: Utility interconnection screens, AI debt issuance and FCF conversion.

developingThemes.name: Food / Grain / Fertilizer Affordability
developingThemes.whyNow: Black Sea rerouting and expensive fuel/freight support food inflation while farm-input demand remains elastic by category.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Premium seed/genetics and nitrogen are harder to defer; potash/phosphate and crop protection have more substitution/deferment; irrigation/machinery remain capex-cyclical.
developingThemes.confirmation: Crop/input ratios and farm margins improve enough to sustain application.
developingThemes.invalidation: Grain/logistics costs fall rapidly while farm economics remain weak.
developingThemes.nextTest: Crop/input ratios, application rates, wheat exports and machinery orders.
developingThemes.action: BG/CTVA/CF quality preferred; AGCO remains second-stage.

developingThemes.name: Physical-Operations Software / Industrial IoT
developingThemes.whyNow: Samsara delivered 30% revenue and ARR growth, 28% net-new ARR growth and a fourth consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter while large-customer adoption deepened.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Provides a differentiated software exposure tied to fleets, logistics, construction and industrial operations rather than generic seat-based SaaS.
developingThemes.confirmation: Large-customer ARR, GAAP profitability and emerging-product adoption keep compounding.
developingThemes.invalidation: Growth slows sharply or valuation outruns cash conversion after the earnings gap.
developingThemes.nextTest: IOT valuation/retest, Q3 guidance execution and FCF margin.
developingThemes.action: NEW PRIORITY RESEARCH; do not chase the post-earnings gap.

developingThemes.name: Selective AI Software / Cybersecurity Monetisation
developingThemes.whyNow: SNOW and cybersecurity vendors show genuine consumption/ARR demand, but rates again raise the valuation hurdle.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Favors measurable ARR/RPO/FCF and mission-critical security over blanket SaaS multiple expansion.
developingThemes.confirmation: AI products lift ARR/RPO and FCF across multiple vendors.
developingThemes.invalidation: Growth depends primarily on multiple expansion without cash conversion.
developingThemes.action: Use pullbacks; do not chase earnings gaps.

developingThemes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel Scarcity
developingThemes.whyNow: Fuel-cycle scarcity remains more investable than concept-stage reactor beta; Iran safeguards tension adds geopolitical fuel-cycle risk but not a new demand step-change.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports operating uranium/fuel names while elevated real yields penalize pre-commercial reactors.
developingThemes.confirmation: Contracting/fuel constraints stay tight and operating assets execute.
developingThemes.invalidation: Fuel supply loosens materially or contracting weakens.

developingThemes.name: Gold / Silver / Monetary Hedge
developingThemes.whyNow: Gold and silver reversed part of the Sep 3 rally after payrolls pushed yields and the dollar higher.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Structural fiscal/geopolitical hedge remains, but real yields and USD dominate near-term entry timing.
developingThemes.confirmation: Bullion holds support despite high real yields or yields roll over after inflation data.
developingThemes.invalidation: Real yields/USD continue higher and bullion loses the rebound structure.
developingThemes.action: Stage only; tactical promotion from Sep 4 is reversed.
